datasets.name: PA-X Peace Agreements Database
datasets.description: Database containing 2257 peace agreements found in more than 170 peace processes between 1990 and the end of 2025, now with 113 new agreements.
datasets.citation: Bell, C., & Badanjak, S. (2019). Introducing PA-X: A new peace agreement database and dataset. Journal of Peace Research, 56(3), 452-466.

datasets.name: Peace Agreement Actor Dataset
datasets.description: Non-local actors/signatories recorded from each peace agreement in PA-X's 'party' and 'third parties' metadata fields; actor IDs may link to UCDP and ACLED actor IDs.

fields.name: signatory_id
fields.label: Signatory ID
fields.description: Unique identifier for the actor-agreement signatory instance (dyad). Unit of analysis.

fields.name: AgtId
fields.label: Agreement ID
fields.description: Unique identifier of the agreement in the PA-X Peace Agreements database.

fields.name: agt_name
fields.label: Agreement Name
fields.description: Name of agreement as per PA-X, and the date agreement signed in brackets.

fields.name: signatory_type
fields.label: Signatory Type
fields.description: Type of signatory to agreement as defined in PA-X, values can be  party  or  third party  depending on the field the actor was listed.

fields.name: practical_third
fields.label: Practical Third Party
fields.description: If the signatory instance by the actor is a third party to the conflict, this field takes the value of 1.

fields.name: condition
fields.label: Condition for Practical Third Party
fields.description: If there is a value of 1 for practical third, this denotes the condition under which it was categorised, as defined by the methodology (values can be C1, C2, C3, C4).

fields.name: actor_id
fields.label: Actor ID
fields.description: Numeric unique identifier of the actor

fields.name: id_paax
fields.label: PAA-X ID
fields.description: Unique identifier for the actor. Primary key. Denotes type and numeric actor ID seperated by '_'

fields.name: actor_name
fields.label: Actor Name
fields.description: Primary name of actor

fields.name: actor_type
fields.label: Actor Type
fields.description: Overall type of actor as per actor definitions. Values can be: 'Country/State', 'Intergovernmental Organization',  'Political Party', 'Entity', 'State Coalition', 'Military',  'Civil Society', 'Armed Organization', 'Umbrella', 'Government/state' and 'Other'.

fields.name: sub_type
fields.label: Actor Sub-Type
fields.description: Actor sub-type which is only applicable to types intergovernmental organisations and civil society. Differentiates regional IGO's, and sub-types of civil society (non-governmental organisations, religious, communities and tribes, government agency and unions).

fields.name: cs_type
fields.label: Civil Society Sub-Group
fields.description: The sub-type 'non-governmental organisation' is further split into - can take values of 'youth', 'women' or 'other'.

fields.name: actor_iso3c
fields.label: Actor Country Based ISO Code
fields.description: ISO 3 character code of the country where the actor is primarily based.

fields.name: actor_country
fields.label: Actor Country Based
fields.description: Country name of where the actor is primarily based.

fields.name: actor_gwno
fields.label: Actor Country Based GWNO
fields.description: Gledistch and Ward digit code of the country where the actor is primarily based.

fields.name: actor_region
fields.label: Actor Region Based
fields.description: Geographic region of the country where the actor is primarily based. If across numerous countries/regions this is left blank.

fields.name: abbreviation
fields.label: Actor Abbreviation
fields.description: Abbreviation of actor name, if applicable

fields.name: un_type
fields.label: Type of UN Actor
fields.description: Type of UN Office/member, if applicable. Possible values include: United Nations, UN Mission, P5 member or none.

fields.name: international
fields.label: International Actor
fields.description: If the actor is an IGO or NGO that acts internationally, they are labelled with a 1.

fields.name: regional
fields.label: Regional Actor
fields.description: If the actor is an IGO or NGO that acts regionally, they are labelled with a 1.

fields.name: domestic
fields.label: Domestic Actor
fields.description: If the actor is a NGO that acts domestically, they are labelled with a 1.

fields.name: women
fields.label: Women Actor
fields.description: If the actor is representing women, they are labelled with a 1.

fields.name: ucdp_id
fields.label: UCDP Actor ID
fields.description: The unique numeric ID of the actor in the UCDP Database: https://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/index.html#actor

fields.name: ucdp_name
fields.label: UCDP Actor Name
fields.description: The name of the actor as recorded in the UCDP Database: https://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/index.html#actor

fields.name: acled_name
fields.label: Primary ACLED Name
fields.description: The name of the actor as recorded in the ACLED Dataset: https://acleddata.com/

fields.name: acled_other
fields.label: Other ACLED Name
fields.description: The alternative name(s) of the actor as recorded in the ACLED Dataset: https://acleddata.com/ . If more than one, separated by a pipe ("|")

fields.name: Con
fields.label: Country/Entity
fields.description: The country or jurisdiction in which the conflict originated; where the conflict has a territorial element, the entity to which the conflict relates according to PA-X.

fields.name: PPName
fields.label: Peace Process
fields.description: Name of peace process according to PA-X. Defined as a formal attempt to bring political and/or military protagonists of conflict, to some sort of mutual agreement as to how to end the conflict, defined broadly as continuing through phases of mediation, unless formally terminated, or a new process has been formally created, taking context into account.

fields.name: Reg
fields.label: Region (Agreement)
fields.description: Region in which the conflict addressed by the agreement is taking place, as listed by PA-X. Regions listed: Africa (excl. MENA), Americas, Asia and Pacific, Europe and Eurasia, Middle East and North Africa, Cross-regional, Other.

fields.name: Dat
fields.label: Date Signed
fields.description: The date on which the agreement was signed or agreed, as recorded by PA-X. Listed in the dataset as YYYY-MM-DD. Sometimes, particularly in the case of  declarations  from meetings, the database contains a date period, e.g. 4-8 May 2015. In this case the last date is entered as the date of the agreement.

fields.name: year
fields.label: Year Signed
fields.description: Year in which the agreement was signed or agreed, extracted from Dat.

fields.name: agt_type
fields.label: Agreement/conflict Type
fields.description: This is a character variable, describing the primary nature of the agreement and conflict as per PA-X Database. Values can be interstate, intrastate or interstate/mixed. Agreements labelled with IntraLocal in PA-X are excluded from this database.

fields.name: stage_process
fields.label: Stage of Process
fields.description: This is a character variable that provides information on the stage of the peace process that the agreement is signed in, assigned by PA-X. Values can be prenegotiation/process;  ceasefire/related; substantive-comprehensive; substantive-partial; implementation/renegotiation; renewal; other.

fields.name: Part
fields.label: Parties
fields.description: Text from the 'Part' field in PA-X. Denotes the parties who directly sign the agreement, often the parties to the conflict and their regional allies. This was coded in  cut and paste  form, exactly as written in the original peace agreement in PA-X.

fields.name: ThrdPart
fields.label: Third Parties
fields.description: Text from the 'ThrdPart' field in PA-X. Denotes parties who sign the agreement as third parties, such as observers, guarantors, or witnesses; these can be states, international organizations, and nongovernmental organizations.

fields.name: Loc1ISO
fields.label: Primary Location ISO
fields.description: Indicates primary location of intrastate conflict and returns the ISO country designation. In cases of interstate conflict, indicates one of the two main locations, assigned randomly to location 1 or location 2. The fields are left empty in cases of agreements that deal with multiple locations and conflicts, such as the Great Lakes Agreements.

fields.name: Loc2ISO
fields.label: Secondary Location ISO
fields.description: Only used in cases of interstate conflict, indicating one of the primary locations of interstate conflict, and returning the ISO country designation. The two main locations are assigned randomly to location 1 or location 2. The exception to this common usage of the variable is in cases of local agreements which deal with cross-border communities and local peace practices therein. In these cases, the locations of both countries are noted, with random assignment of each to Location 1 or Location 2.

fields.name: Loc1GWNO
fields.label: Primary Location GWNO
fields.description: Indicates primary location of intrastate conflict and returns the Gleditsch-Ward country code. In cases of interstate conflict, indicates one of the two main locations, assigned randomly to location 1 or location 2. The fields are left empty in cases of agreements that deal with multiple locations and conflicts, such as the Great Lakes Agreements. For more on GWNO codes, see: Gleditsch, Kristian S., and Michael D. Ward. 1999.  Interstate System Membership: A Revised List of the Independent States since 1816.  International Interactions 25(4): 393 413.

fields.name: Loc2GWNO
fields.label: Secondary Location GWNO
fields.description: Only used in cases of interstate conflict, indicating one of the primary locations of interstate conflict, and returning the Gleditsch-Ward country code. The two main locations are assigned randomly to location 1 or location 2. The exception to this common usage of the variable is in cases of local agreements which deal with crossborder communities and local peace practices therein. In these cases, the locations of both countries are noted, with random assignment of each to Location 1 or Location 2. For more on GWNO codes, see: Gleditsch, Kristian S., and Michael D. Ward. 1999.  Interstate System Membership: A Revised List of the Independent States since 1816.  International Interactions 25(4): 393 413.

fields.name: UcdpCon
fields.label: UCDP Conflict ID
fields.description: Uppsala Conflict Data Program Conflict ID. Note that the Conflict IDs applied are from 2017 and onward, after the UCDP introduced a new system of conflict designation. It is possible that this field is empty this happens in cases of conflicts not registered in the UCDP conflict data. For more information on the UCDP data and conflict codes and definition see: Pettersson, Ther se, and Kristine Eck. 2018.  Organized Violence, 1989 2017.  Journal of Peace Research 55(4): 535 47. Also see http://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/

fields.name: UcdpAgr
fields.label: UCDP Agreement ID
fields.description: Uppsala Conflict Data Program peace agreement ID. For more information on these data, see H gbladh, Stina. 2011.  Peace Agreements 1975-2011 - Updating the UCDP Peace Agreement Dataset Peace in the UCDP Dataset.  States in Armed Conflict 2011: Uppsala University: Department of Peace and Conflict Research Report 99: 39 56

fields.name: PamAgr
fields.label: PAM Agreement ID
fields.description: Kroc Institute s Peace Accords Matrix agreement ID. It is possible that this field is empty   this happens in cases of agreements not part of the PAM data. The PAM focuses on comprehensive agreements only, so the bulk of PA-X documents do not have the PAM agreement code. For more information on PAM, see: Joshi, Madhav, Jason Michael Quinn, and Patrick M Regan. 2015.  Annualized Implementation Data on Comprehensive Intrastate Peace Accords, 1989 2012.  Journal of Peace Research 52(4): 551 62. http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0022343314567486.

fields.name: CowWar
fields.label: COW War Number
fields.description: Correlates of War: War Number. Many PA-X agreements come from peace processes in conflicts that do not meet the high battle-related deaths criterion of the Correlates of War project, so the war numbers are not provided for many of the agreements. For more information on the Correlates of War war list, see: Sarkees, Meredith Reid, and Frank Whelon. Wayman. 2010. Resort to War : A Data Guide to Inter-State, Extra-State, Intra-State, and Non-State Wars, 1816-2007. Washington D.C.: CQ Press.

fields.name: PAX_Hyperlink
fields.label: PA-X Agreement URL
fields.description: URL link to the coding page of the agreement on PA-X Database.

fields.name: PDF_Hyperlink
fields.label: PDF Full Text URL
fields.description: URL link to the translated PDF of the agreement text on PA-X Database.

datasets.name: Peace Agreement Amnesties Dataset
datasets.description: PA-X agreements recoded for amnesty provisions, excluding localised agreements, domestic-rules-only provisions, unilateral texts, and agreements that only restate an amnesty commitment made in an earlier agreement.
datasets.citation: Mallinder, Louise. 2026. "Peace Agreement Amnesties Dataset." Harvard Dataverse. https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/FVKC79
datasets.notes: UNCERTAIN structure: local file Peace_Agreement_Amnesties_Dataset_10_Oct_2025.xlsx's 'Full Peace Agreement Coding' sheet (the main data sheet) does not have a clean single header row — row 1 mixes real column labels (Country, Year, Peace Agreement Name) with what are actually data values from other rows (e.g. a full agreement-text excerpt appears as a 'column header'), consistent with this being a flattened/pasted pivot-table export rather than tidy tabular data. Other sheets in the workbook (Sheet1/3/4/8, 'No countries by region', etc.) are small pivot-summary outputs, not raw data. `fields` left empty rather than fabricated from this structure — flagging for a manual look rather than guessing which row is the real header.
